1. Leonardo da Vinci - the famous Renaissance artist, inventor, and thinker.

2. Marie Curie - the pioneering physicist and chemist who made groundbreaking discoveries in the field of radioactivity.

3. Mahatma Gandhi - the influential leader who fought for Indian independence and civil rights through nonviolent resistance.

4. William Shakespeare - the renowned playwright and poet who remains one of the most widely studied and performed writers in history.

5. Isaac Newton - the English mathematician and physicist who is widely regarded as one of the most influential scientists in history.

6. Alexander the Great - the famous ancient Macedonian king who conquered much of the known world.

7. Cleopatra - the powerful Egyptian queen who ruled during a time of great turmoil and conflict.

8. Albert Einstein - the German-born physicist who is best known for his theory of relativity and other groundbreaking contributions to the field of physics.

9. Nelson Mandela - the anti-apartheid revolutionary and former President of South Africa who fought for racial equality and justice.

10. Jane Austen - the acclaimed English novelist who wrote timeless works such as "Pride and Prejudice" and "Sense and Sensibility".
